files.citation: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd ed., 1855, Table 1: attacks and deaths by date, Broad Street outbreak. Digitised in the HistData R package (Friendly) as Snow.dates; retrieved as CSV through Rdatasets.
files.note: Outbreak-wide daily totals, not per-address counts: these figures cannot be joined to cholera_deaths.csv case by case, and the two files do not agree on a total because they count different things. Dated rows carry 571 attacks and 616 deaths between 1854-08-19 and 1854-09-30; one row carries 45 attacks of unknown date and no date value. Attacks peak on 1854-09-01 and deaths on 1854-09-02, which is why a series must state which kind of date it uses. The underlying table is from an 1855 publication; the retrieval route is recorded for provenance rather than as a licence claim over historical facts.

transforms: CSV FID prefixed for stable point IDs; original attributes retained; coordinates unchanged
GraphML directed edges retain endpoints, length and WKT geometry; other tags omitted

snow_dates.csv is bundled exactly as retrieved, so its digest matches the source. Its final row has an empty date, which a keyed table cannot represent, so a workflow importing it excludes that row and states the 45 attacks of unknown date that are therefore absent.
